what_happened: This job was a retry of an earlier job (20261106-042815-ntc7) that widened the ontology-term check to scan all governing docs. The verifier rejected it. Two of six acceptance criteria were unmet. First, decision D152 in docs/decisions.md still says the check scans only BRIEF.md and the term's file sources, and no decision should keep that narrower scope. Second, the real-file ontology test with the full cargo checks was not shown to pass. The findings include one blocker: the new D160 entry breaks the backtest decision-log check at docs/decisions.md:4441, so cargo test fails. They also include a major finding that D160 wrongly says no decision keeps the narrow scope while D152 still does, a major finding that criterion 6's evidence must cite commands that ran (D43), and a major finding that the reading does not match the request. One check ran and failed: test. Its kept output is only CI cleanup and a Node.js warning, so the failing test is not visible. The job added a new decision entry instead of amending D152, and that entry broke a decisions-format test.
cause: Nothing ties a behavior change to the decision records that describe that behavior. The first attempt (20261106-042756-h268) was rejected for exactly this: D152 left unamended. The retry's reading did not carry that finding forward as a required end state, so D152 was again left standing. The producer added a new entry, D160, in place of amending D152. The entry's format was not run against the decision-log test before the final verdict, and its claim that no decision keeps the old scope was not checked against D152. The failed test check's kept output is CI noise, so the producer and verifier could not see which assertion failed. The reading also misread the request, which made the passing criteria weak evidence.
prevention: Add a check that runs when a job edits code or behavior covered by docs/decisions.md. It would find the existing decisions that mention the changed behavior, for example by searching for the file or check name, and fail unless each is amended or explicitly confirmed. It would also check that any new decision entry passes the decision-log format test and does not claim "no decision keeps X" while a grep finds one that does. For retries, the reading must copy the prior verifier's unmet criteria and major findings in as required end states. The test check should also keep the failing test name and assertion, not only CI cleanup.
proposed_request: Retry of 20261106-042815-ntc7 and 20261102-223344-sqs9. The ontology-term check must scan BRIEF.md, README.md, every docs/*.md and the term's file sources, not only BRIEF.md and the term's file sources. Outcomes: (1) Amend decision D152 in docs/decisions.md in place so it states this wider scan scope. Do not add a new decision that claims D152 is gone, and make sure no other decision in docs/decisions.md still states the narrower scope. Search the file for the old scope wording and reconcile every hit. (2) If you add any new decision entry, make it pass the existing decision-log format test (the backtest decision-log check) and link it to the amended decision. Run cargo test locally first. (3) Add a CHANGELOG.md entry that describes only what the diff does. (4) The real-file ontology test must pass on docs/ontology.toml with no new excuses. Run cargo test -p athena-cli --test ontology, then cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test, and cite the commands you ran in the report. Do not change anything else.
